chunk_list: SILEX PILOT FINAL EVALUATION REPORT V1.0 1. Executive summary The final SILEX pilot evaluation was conducted with ten participants from the Santa Marina City Council between 7 and 14 October 2026. Participants represented citizen services, urban planning, trade, environment, the general secretariat, and electronic administration. Every participant completed six procedure-search and review tasks followed by a questionnaire and short interview. Evaluation measured success, time, requests for help, clarity, ease of search, ES/EN consistency, and confidence in deadlines and legal bases. The overall success rate was 88%. Median task time was 2 minutes 18 seconds. Language switching preserved the query and entity in 100% of journeys. The API achieved p95 latency of 1.42 seconds during sessions. No exposure of restricted data was identified. 2. Scope Tasks covered locating a procedure, identifying the competent unit, checking a channel, interpreting a deadline, comparing a legal version, and switching language. Authorized procedures and data without personal cases were used.

The evaluation does not measure large-scale citizen use and does not replace a complete accessibility audit. Results apply to the environment, corpus, and versions recorded in the manifest. 3. Method Tasks had verifiable answers and success criteria. Five participants began in Spanish and five in English. Order was alternated to reduce learning effects. Observers recorded actions and assistance but not the content of personal searches. Comments were classified by severity, frequency, and scope. A critical defect blocked the pilot; a major defect required priority correction; a minor defect could move to the improvement plan. Evaluation section 1 Task 1 was to locate a minor building permit. The objective was to search by text and verify that the correct record appears among the first results. Complete success, partial success, failure, time, action count, assistance, and comments were recorded. Review compared the answer with the source and distinguished a data, interface, wording, or training defect. Results were analyzed by language and profile.
